title: Disentangled Multi-interest Representation Learning for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation needs to model users' complex multi-interest preferences from behavioral data.

gap.claim: Existing distinct representations for users' interests can collapse into similar representations because of insufficient guidance.

contributions.claim: A generic sequential-recommendation method for disentangled representation learning of diverse user interests.
A global co-purchase-likelihood-guided item partition that encourages each item group to focus on a discriminated interest.
An MRF-based sub-graph sampling optimization approach combined with multi-task alignment of item partition learning and multi-interest modeling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world datasets reportedly show significant improvement over state-of-the-art methods.
The method reportedly integrates flexibly with existing multi-interest models as a plugin and enhances their performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets accurate modeling of users' complex multi-interest preferences.
Existing multi-interest representations are vulnerable to collapse because effective guidance is lacking.
The authors propose a generic method for disentangled multi-interest representation learning.
The method uses co-purchase-guided item partitioning, a spectral-clustering connection, MRF-based optimization, contrastive learning, and multi-task alignment.
The authors report improvements on three real-world datasets and plugin benefits for existing models.
